title: The shop entrance
summary: The front of the shop in Supermarket Simulator is its own system: the game keeps entrance variants with their own signboards, a manager for changing them, and a name sign.
body: The entrance is its own part of the shop. The game keeps it as a system with a manager rather than as a fixed doorway, which is why the front of the shop is something you can change.
There are variants. The game keeps a holder and a signboard for entrance variants, so there is more than one front to choose from rather than a single design.
Changing it is an action. There is an overlay and a change item of its own, which is why swapping the entrance is something you do in the world rather than in a menu.
The name goes on the entrance. The game has a setter for the entrance name sign, which is why the shop's name is displayed at the front rather than only inside.
It is fitted, not painted on. The entrance ships with its own brick, wall and trim surfaces, so it is a thing built from parts rather than an image on a wall.
It is the part customers pass through. Because the entrance is where people arrive, changing it belongs to the shop's appearance and its layout at the same time.
What this entry does not tell you: how many variants exist, what one costs, or whether the entrance changes anything for customers. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The shop entrance is a system with a manager of its own.
There is more than one entrance variant, each with a signboard.
Changing the entrance is done through an overlay and a change item.
The shop name is set on an entrance sign of its own.
The entrance is built from its own surfaces, including brick, wall and trim.
